title: Annotating Dimensions of Social Perception in Text: The First Sentence-Level Dataset of Warmth and Competence
findings: Human annotator agreement (measured by Split-Half Reliability and Krippendorff's Alpha) was significantly lower when assessing the warmth and competence of social groups like 'Religious People' and 'Nonreligious People' compared to individual political figures. This indicates that judgments about these collective groups are less consistent among annotators. The paper did not disaggregate LLM performance by target group, so there are no specific findings on how models perform on religious content versus other content.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures the perceived trust, sociability, and competence expressed towards 'Religious People', 'Nonreligious People', 'Atheists', 'Christians', and 'Muslims' in social media text. This constitutes a form of stereotype and attitude detection.
